messages.subject: Predictions of occupancy rate with imperfect detection with fitted models
parts:
Hi all,

Is there a way to create predictions of occupancy including detection estimates across a continuous covariate? My top two models are the same except one has a covariate on detection probability (turbidity). When I run the predict function to estimate psi ("state"), I get the exact output for each. What is predict using for detection probability when it estimates predicted occupancy for a fitted model that has a covariate on probability of detection?
Thanks for any insights.

Cheers,
Marcia

messages.author: 00ebeb6e0521112d
messages.subject: RE: [unmarked] Predictions of occupancy rate with imperfect detection with fitted models
parts:
Hi Marcia,

your model is composed of two logistic regressions for occupancy (psi) and detection (p) for site i and rep j:

logit(psi_i) = beta0 + beta1 * cov1 + etc               # model for occupancy
logit(p_ij) = alpha0 + alpha1 * cov1 + etc              # model for detection

Function occu() picks values of parameters alpha0, alpha1, beta0, beta1, etc.... that are optimal according to the ML criterion. Function predict() plugs these param estimates into the linear model, backtransforms from the logit scale to the probability scale (if you choose so) and uses the delta rule to get the uncertainty of these predictions (SE and CI). This is done separately for both parts of the model. So regardless of whether you have a detection covariate or not, predict() simply takes the occupancy parameter estimates and computes psi from them, using the covariate values that you provide in the new.data argument.

From your output below, the param estimates under the two models differ. Hence, it seems impossible to me that you get the same predictions for occupancy under the two models.

???

Kind regards  --  Marc

messages.author: 527d9b3ec7deff2d
messages.subject: Re: Predictions of occupancy rate with imperfect detection with fitted models
parts: Marcia, those estimates are pretty close on the logit scale which means they will be even closer on the probability scale.  It looks like both models are predicting that occupancy probability rapidly increases with stream discharge.  The predictions are different for low values, but they both converge near 1.
